what_worked: Sharp thesis, tight narrative arc, excellent visual restraint, and a genuinely memorable title.
fix_next: Multiple median figures are wrong (AI $446 vs $503, Education $2,142 vs $2,435, B2B 5.7× vs ~2.35×); verify every number against the dataset.
verdict: Strong storytelling undermined by several material numerical errors.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1/3: AI median stated $446, reference is $503. Slide 1/3: Education median stated $2,142, reference is $2,435. Slide 3/4: B2B vs B2C multiplier stated 5.7×, reference median multiple is ~2.35×. Slide 3: 'Customer Support' and 'Marketplace' categories with specific medians ($5,163, $4,322) do not appear in the reference category list—possibly fabricated or from uncategorized subsets with tiny n.

evidence.insight: Core insight (crowded AI underperforms boring B2B categories on median MRR) is genuinely useful and non-obvious, but analysis stays shallow—no discussion of sample sizes, survivorship, or why medians diverge. Only two data dimensions explored (category count vs median revenue, B2B/B2C split).
evidence.narrative: Excellent four-slide arc: hook (title), evidence of crowding (slide 2), revenue contrast (slide 3), actionable takeaway (slide 4). Each slide builds on the prior. The 'it's early' framing on slide 4 adds nuance.
evidence.framing: Dataset source and freeze date stated clearly. However, 274 missing category values (~27%) are never mentioned, which materially affects the 'crowded' claim. Audience is implied (indie builders) but never explicitly stated. No limitations slide.
evidence.accuracy: AI median off by ~$57 ($446 vs $503). Education median off by ~$293 ($2,142 vs $2,435). B2B/B2C 5.7× multiplier is dramatically wrong—reference shows ~2.35× median. 'Customer Support' and 'Marketplace' categories with stated medians don't appear in the reference dataset at all, raising fabrication concerns. The n=1,000 source note is correct but misleadingly implies all 1,000 are categorized.
evidence.visual: Clean, consistent dark palette with gold/rust accent. Horizontal bar charts are well-chosen and properly labeled. Good use of callout boxes. Typography hierarchy is clear. No chartjunk. Slight issue: slide 3 bar chart shows only 6 of 12+ categories, cherry-picking the contrast.
